Listen, something strange is happening here! I can’t write now, just come to Coldberg, Swindlerville immediately. I’ll tell you everything. Hurry up, we don’t have much time.

When writing a book, the hardest thing is to start. I've been sitting over this scroll for an hour, chewing on my quill, and I still haven't come up with a good preamble.

Here's the thing: I have a journal, everyone knows about it, it was even printed, but they didn't do a good job: they printed many copies of the first pages, but not enough copies of the last ones. But those events were written down by some scribe the way he heard them, I'm not the one who told him about Umoir.

And here I'm summoned by Skrakan - the one I've served for who knows how many years - and says: you've been places, Danas. And now rest a bit and write down your account of everything that happened to you...

Read Danas's Guide to Allods to view the contents of the page.

name.en: Page 1 of Danas's Guide to Allods: Why I wrote it.

description.en:
I told you how surprised I was when representatives of our countries sat down and started working together...

But there is one place in Sarnaut where the animosity between Kania and Xadagan has no importance...

It's an incredible place - the Ark allod where the great mage Erast rules...

Read Danas's Guide to Allods to view the contents of the page.

name.en: Page 10 of Danas's Guide to Allods. Ark.

description.en:
First I'll tell you about my home allod - the Kanian Archipelagos.

Our land is beautiful. Green meadows, thick forests, bottomless lakes, and high mountains. We have everything.

But most importantly, we have our capital city - Kania. That's how it is...

Read Danas's Guide to Allods to view the contents of the page.

name.en: Page 2 of Danas's Guide to Allods. Kanian Archipelagos.

description.en:
The next allod is Grok. We visited it when Skrakan asked us to deliver a message to Claude de Vevre - the elven Great Mage that controls that allod.

As you know, elves prefer to keep away from humans. They guard their secrets, and they dislike foreigners. They also live on Umoir... Somewhere beyond Al Rihat, if I remember correctly. They trade and sell what they make. But they are a small House...

Read Danas's Guide to Allods to view the contents of the page.

name.en: Page 3 of Danas's Guide to Allods. Grok.

description.en:
Last time I told you about the elven allod where elves live alongside orcs, and now I'm going to tell you about the allod where elves reign over the land, and yet Kanians also live there.

Grok's Great Mage is Claude de Vevre, but Andis is controlled by his cousin - Catherine de Vevre...

Read Danas's Guide to Allods to view the contents of the page.

name.en: Page 4 of Danas's Guide to Allods. Andis.

description.en:
You probably want to ask me - have you been to Xadaganian allods, Danas?

I'll be honest - I have. My duties took me to Igsh...

Read Danas's Guide to Allods to view the contents of the page.

name.en: Page 5 of Danas's Guide to Allods. Igsh.

description.en:
After hearing my stories about the elves of the House de Vevre, you probably think that most elves are arrogant bastards.

But it's not true. All their Houses are different...

Read Danas's Guide to Allods to view the contents of the page.

name.en: Page 6 of Danas's Guide to Allods. Yoggor.

description.en:
We visited an unusual Xadaganian allod later.

At the time, Nezeb's Falcons were hunting down disloyal Great Mages... They took out Vodor of Arav, Kadir of Igsh, Rashid of Sulanger... The Xadaganian Emperor replaced them all with his loyal allies.

Read Danas's Guide to Allods to view the contents of the page.

name.en: Page 7 of Danas's Guide to Allods. Yakhch

description.en:
I told you about elven and Xadaganian allods, but you probably want to hear about Kanian ones, too.

But that's the thing - Kania is right there, outside your window. Look! And it doesn't matter if it's Kanian Archipelagos, Umoir, or Forox - it's the same everywhere.

Read Danas's Guide to Allods to view the contents of the page.

There are so many books in Skytower - it will take many lifetimes to read them. But there's a place with even more books. There's a collector among the Great Mages who collects various antiquities. And the book that's more valuable to him than anything else is the one he has yet to get his hands on...

Read Danas's Guide to Allods to view the contents of the page.

name.en: Page 9 of Danas's Guide to Allods. Ney.

description.en:
I'm afraid the news are true, my friend!

Tensess is dead, and not only him - the losses are hard to describe, we are dealing with something worse than the Black Night...

The people already named it the Night of Astral Portals...

Read Skrakan's Archive to view the contents of the page.

name.en: Letter 10 from Skrakan's Archive. A Letter from Great Mage Gorluxor to Skrakan

description.en:
Skrakan, my friend!

I wrote to you as soon I received the news. I'm afraid your worry is warranted. Exploration of other words could be dangerous. The Conclave has a very vague idea of what could await us there... I suppose we should consider them hostile...

Read Skrakan's Archive to view the contents of the page.

name.en: Letter 2 from Skrakan's Archive. A Letter from Great Mage Maive to Skrakan

description.en:
Skrakan, my friend and mentor!

I'm afraid I have bad news. It's about Nezeb, of course.

Here at the desert border, I hear reports of what is happening.

Read Skrakan's Archive to view the contents of the page.

name.en: Letter 3 from Skrakan's Archive. A Letter from Great Mage Yokke to Skrakan.

description.en:
Oh, Great Skrakan! Allow this servant to send you a letter!

I am Kahhar, a humble servant of my Emperor, praise his name, may it be exalted forever, and may the sun shine bright over the Xadaganian Empire...!

Read Skrakan's Archive to view the contents of the page.

name.en: Letter 4 from Skrakan's Archive. A Letter from Great Mage Kakhar to Skrakan

description.en:
Skrakan, my friend!

I'm torn with doubts as I'm writing this. Soon we'll be ready for the Great Experiment.

You know how long it took to prepare... It was a great effort to gather everyone...

Read Skrakan's Archive to view the contents of the page.

name.en: Letter 6 from Skrakan's Archive. A Letter from Great Mage Zayan to Skrakan

description.en:
Skrakan!

It's a catastrophe! A complete and absolute failure! We were so foolish...

The world is breaking apart... Something's devouring it... something I can't even name. This substance... cannot be controlled...

Read Skrakan's Archive to view the contents of the page.

name.en: Letter 7 from Skrakan's Archive. A Letter from Great Mage Tensess to Skrakan

description.en:
Oh, wise Skrakan!

I'm glad to report that my observations have been confirmed. The Astral was stopped, the stasis spell is holding.

We saved the world, but the price was high. I'm afraid, the truth about what really happened will ruin us all...

Read Skrakan's Archive to view the contents of the page.

name.en: Letter 8 from Skrakan's Archive. A Letter from Great Mage Aidenus to Skrakan

description.en:
Skrakan, my dear friend!

For years, I've tried to understand what you dealt with in the Outer Worlds, and what caused you to seal your allod in frantic haste. One thing is certain - you are alive, and you have encountered a great threat.

Read Skrakan's Archive to view the contents of the page.

name.en: Letter 9 from Skrakan's Archive. A Letter from Great Mage Tensess to Skrakan and all the attached documents.

description.en:
Many people treat dark arts with mistrust, and with good reason. Summoners of the old earned an ill name, and of course, the first one that comes to mind is Tep who doomed his people. But there were others, too...

Read Yazes's Chronicles and Urd's Notes to view the contents of the page.

No one trusts dark mages. No one believed them then either, but they managed to persuade the king to allow them to form their own organization in exchange for an artifact - a crown that protects its owner against the magic of the Astral. It became a guarantee for the king that he will be protected against any possible influence that might come from the guild...

Read Yazes's Chronicles and Urd's Notes to view the contents of the page.

Iglez governed one of the villages on Yazes called Lairisha. That was where he and Galenel first ran into Urd's Summoners. Back then, Urd was already gathering an army for an attack on Xadagan, but he still needed recruits for his undead horde. The recruitment process was rough: they took everyone they could, ignoring pleas and protests...

Read Yazes's Chronicles and Urd's Notes to view the contents of the page.

name.en: Page 3 of Yazes's Chronicles. Three stars.

description.en:
Heed this warning, one who reads this scroll, and beware - for you are on a dark path.

This is a Summoner's craft - the art of controlling the dead. This knowledge has been forbidden for centuries, so beware of delving into its secrets, because the Conclave's rules are strict, and those who violate them will be severely punished...

Read Yazes's Chronicles and Urd's Notes to view the contents of the page.

name.en: Page 1 of Urd's Notes. About the undead.

description.en:
We have talked about the undead that have no Sparks, but there are some who do. There is nothing difficult about summoning a Spark and trapping it in an already dead body.

But there is a kind of undead that are not easy to create – ghosts. A ghost is a result of magic – powerful curses that rip the Spark from the afterlife and bind it to a certain place or object...

Read Yazes's Chronicles and Urd's Notes to view the contents of the page.

name.en: Page 2 of Urd's Notes. About ghosts.

description.en:
It is time to talk about controlling the undead magic.

A powerful summoner can sustain numerous undead, but there is a question of control. The undead do not take kindly to being disturbed, and it is very difficult to force them to obey...

Read Yazes's Chronicles and Urd's Notes to view the contents of the page.

name.en: Page 3 of Urd's Notes. How to build an undead army.

description.en:
History has examples for any kind of situation. Unfortunately, sometimes her lessons are too bitter – so we prefer to forget what happened. That's how it went with the events that darkened the existence of elves soon after the Change...

Read the History of Vampires to view the contents of the page.

name.en: Page 1 of the History of Vampires. Children of the Dark.

description.en:
Those events are now known as the Blood Feast. The kingdom was divided, so no one felt safe, and each night was full of terror as people expected to be torn apart by monsters who had recently been their friends, colleagues, or even family...

Read the History of Vampires to view the contents of the page.

name.en: Page 2 of the History of Vampires. Blood Feast.

description.en:
The fate of Canaan and his vampire followers has been kept secret for ages.

Still, the vampires appeared here and there, and both humans and elves feared them. The Aro tribes encountered them first...

Read the History of Vampires to view the contents of the page.

name.en: Page 3 of the History of Vampires. Canaan's fate.

description.en:
The Galleon Castle. A miracle of engineering created by the House de Ardeur. Many are interested in how this place came to be. Well, it's no great mystery... the mystery is how it turned into the Darkblood Citadel...

Read the History of Vampires to view the contents of the page.

name.en: Page 4 of the History of Vampires. Darkblood Citadel

description.en:
During the last Great Ball, the House de Desirae gained a victory. Young prince Dakkar ensured it. He was a Summoner. He won the competition against the head of the House de Doucer, Armando. Even though any foul play was forbidden, Armando still took it as a great insult.

Read the History of Vampires to view the contents of the page.

name.en: Page 5 of the History of Vampires Armando's betrayal.

description.en:
But the House de Doucer wasn't the only family to fall prey to vampires. A similar thing happened to the House de Tristesse. Originally, de Tristesse lived on Umoir, to the east of the market town Al Rihat. Under Skrakan's rule, they traded with humans and did not bother anyone...

Read the History of Vampires to view the contents of the page.

name.en: Page 6 of the History of Vampires Tragedy of the House de Tristesse.

description.en:
The Great Skrakan is wise and clever. He ruled over Umoir since ancient times, and he was a reasonable and fair ruler.

The world was divided between two states, two Empires: Kania and Xadagan, ruled by Skrakan's apprentices, but the Great Mage himself kept out of their conflicts...

Read Legends of Veligrad to view the contents of the page.

name.en: Page 1 of Legends of Veligrad. How Skrakan dreamt about finding other worlds.

description.en:
Everyone knows the story of how Skrakan summoned a Demon.

Umoir was under a seal of secrecy for seventy years before the Great Mage was rescued.

Read Legends of Veligrad to view the contents of the page.

name.en: Page 2 of Legends of Veligrad. About the founding of Veligrad.

description.en:
Over time, Veligrad grew large and prosperous, while its residents looked warily at the sorceress's tower near the city. They knew dark secrets were kept there.

Sorcerers and sorceresses, Galenel's apprentices, visited the city and spread rumors. They said Urd himself was buried somewhere near the tower, and that there were catacombs under the city - with graves where Skrakan and Galenel hid their secrets.

Read Legends of Veligrad to view the contents of the page.

name.en: Page 3 of Legends of Veligrad. How Skrakan learned about Tka-Rik.

description.en:
All was well, but then another trouble arrived. Orcs, goblins, and cyclops lived on Umoir since ancient times... Their numbers changed from year to year, they usually lived in forests, sometimes robbing travelers, even though guards kept them mostly in check.

But they weren't a real threat until a giant named Leviathan gathered them to form a Horde...

Read Legends of Veligrad to view the contents of the page.

name.en: Page 4 of Legends of Veligrad. How Veligrad fell.

description.en:
The tower held many valuables when it fell. The Scroll of Tensess was among them - the one that freed Skrakan. And Tensess's coat as well.

Everything was stolen by marauders. Then witches came to the ruins. Before, they watched the tower's treasures with envy, but now that it was unprotected, they rushed to get their hands on the valuables...

Read Legends of Veligrad to view the contents of the page.

name.en: Page 5 of Legends of Veligrad. About the new Queen of Umoir.

description.en:
The people of Clear Valley have always been Old Believers. They were partially influenced by the Guardian Ring that watched the woods and erected idols of the Sage, Warrior, Hunter, Master, and Maiden.

The new Queen did not like that. And if the first years of her rule were spent developing technomagic, building shipyards, smithies, and schools, over time she decided to lead everyone to the Light...

Read Legends of Veligrad to view the contents of the page.

name.en: Page 6 of Legends of Veligrad. How Clear Valley became Foul.

description.en:
We'll begin our story.

The Kanian nation is old, and no one knows where it originated. It is only known that, when Yul still existed, they lived in the northern forests and swamps full of game. Some nations kept away, because few knew the way through the deadly marshes.

Read the Chronicle of the Valirs to view the contents of the page.

name.en: Page 1 of the Chronicle of the Valirs. Where the Kanian land came from.

description.en:
Oh, the beautiful and bright Kanian land! You astonish with your beauty: numerous lakes, deep rivers, steep mountains, high hills, vast woods, lovely fields, various animals and birds, great cities, lovely villages, noble masters, respectable lords and ladies – you offer so much, Kanian land...!

Read the Chronicle of the Valirs to view the contents of the page.

name.en: Page 2 of the Chronicle of the Valirs. Where the Horde came from.

description.en:
That was a time of great sorrow. When the Horde came, many cities fell, many nations and tribes disappeared, and so worry and fear spread among the people of Aro. It was difficult to watch us. And our joy turned to sorrow. In all towns and villages, people wept and wept aloud.

Read the Chronicle of the Valirs to view the contents of the page.

name.en: Page 3 of the Chronicle of the Valirs. How the Kanian land was ravaged.

description.en:
It took a great effort to defeat the orcs. Many feats were accomplished, and many glorious battles were fought.

At the beginning, kings and sorcerers gathered an army and defeated the orcs that plundered the land, and they were led by Skulnar's son - the cursed Stormrider the Northwind.

Valir defeated Stormrider...

Read the Chronicle of the Valirs to view the contents of the page.

name.en: Page 4 of the Chronicle of the Valirs. Where the Valir dynasty originated.

description.en:
When old Skulnar heard the news, he became so angry he slaughtered all his servants and howled like wolf, because he had only one son left. Skulnar decided to gather a new army that would be more terrifying than the Horde...

Read the Chronicle of the Valirs to view the contents of the page.

name.en: Page 5 of the Chronicle of the Valirs. How Kania was saved.

description.en:
The war with the orcs was over, and Kanian cities grew even more prosperous. They had other enemies to deal with - Lamias, Mantes, and on occasion, a completely different foe.

Back then, elves were divided - their mages fought among themselves for some reason. So the Conclave had empty seats - and the elves admitted the Skrakan first, and then Tensess with Nezeb...

Read the Chronicle of the Valirs to view the contents of the page.

name.en: Page 6 of the Chronicle of the Valirs. About Kanian nobility and conflicts.

description.en:
Dear Captain Grotto!

I hope my order will be completed on time? I would like to note right away that I shall not accept any excuses. This order is extremely important for the realization of my plans, so I would rather not hear excuses and justifications.

If you fail to fulfill my order, I will take back the down payment and make sure to take action that will properly motivate any future contractors who will be fulfilling my orders. I believe you UNDERSTAND what this means for you personally.

Best regards.

An ancient page torn from a book served as a material for the letter. On one side, you see doodles by some goblins, and on the other - ancient writings written carefully by a true master chronicler.

You should show this page to someone who knows a thing or two about ancient legends.

These are the orders given to Tep Cultists. Upon skimming through the papers, you have understood that the mission of the cultist moles at ZIT was to steal some valuable equipment from the sealed crypt and to capture those who will show too much interest in their activities.

Will work only on Distorted Killer Hares!

You can obtain these mines from Maxim Maximov at the Fortecia or from Alexander Suvorov in Hirkalla's palace.

If there is a hare within 5 yards of the mine, it will explode and kill the hare.
The contents look rather indecent... Well, the games in Hickut were rather "peculiar", especially right before the Plague. "Maybe the Plague was the punishment for their sins?", you think.

Decorative pet.

The larvae of this dragonfly live in the warm waters of the tropical atoll for twelve years before they emerge onto land to be reborn and become the most beautiful creatures of summer.

Can be obtained from Jack Cheap at the Tropical Atoll.

The letter is written in large block letters. It contains grammar and spelling mistakes. Whoever wrote this, writing wasn't their thing.

One more translation of another part of this story:

"And then the Dark, as the Junes call him, spoke to them:

He said, 'Oh, the Junes! Sarn told you to kill all dragens. Did he tell you what awaits you afterwards?'

The Junes were confused. They didn't know how to reply.

'You see, the very second you kill the last dragen, this world will cease to exist. Of course, Sarn will be set free. But you all are going to die!'

The Junes then asked what the Dark was suggesting.

'I will give you the choice that Sarn didn't give you. You may choose to keep the promise you gave Sarn, and die together with Sarnaut. Or you could as well forget about the dragen hunt!'

The Junes then asked if Nihaz could protect them from Sarn's wrath.

'I don't fear Sarn! Behold the Star Gates through which I travel between the worlds... Should there be danger, I will give you a new world, and you'll be your own masters!'
The Junes then renounced their promise. They gave their reply to the Dark in the place, where the magic power of the world spilled and transformed into thousands of elementals. This is where the June Curse was born!"

A train of images passes through your mind as you touch this artifact: the Junes, fighting a thousand bloody battles with dragons. The losses are huge, but the hatred is so hot that no one cares to stop. One after another, the Great Dragons, Keepers of the Prison, fall before the growing power. The first among the dragon persecutors is Tka-Rik, the greatest mage that Sarnaut has ever seen.

Finally, eight of the Great Dragons are dead. There's only one left. He's hiding in the mountains like a coward. It won't be long until he's killed, and the Junes fulfill their pledge. But the night comes when the darkness thickens and turns into a monster that has no name. The flustered Junes face it in the ancient city near the source of celestial iron.

There's a competition depicted on the stamp: people with the same stamps jump along rectangular blocks. The winner on the last column is holding up a table above their head. It looks like a call to action, but you can't figure out, which action.

The elven instructions allow you to decipher the June tablet:

"Once there was a young man. He lived in a village. Like all men of his age, he liked young girls. There was a girl from the neighboring village that he was seeing at nights.

The night was quiet, only maize was rustling under the moon, and a cowardly ocelot was sneaking along the creek. The man and the girl were in love. Nothing could stop them that night.

But wind suddenly picked up. It was furious like a hurricane! It bent century-old trees and stripped away water reed from roofs. That was an unusual wind.

The man was peering into darkness. Suddenly, a bright light appeared, as if the sun came up. Those were the flames breathed out by a horrendous fire dragon. Both villages turned to ash in a heartbeat. The fire dragon disappeared.

When the real sun came up, the young man and the girl left the smoldering ruins. The road to the nearest city passed through the dryland. To the city of Uskul."

name.en: Ancient June tablet with a story about a man and a girl from a remote village

description.en:
The tablet translation goes:

"The young man and the girl called the ruler for action. How could anyone put up with the fire dragon's attacks?

But the wise ruler Witzliwitle laughed and said,

'You may be brave, but you're stupid. A man is weak. A man can never fight a mighty fire dragon!'

But the young man and the girl called to avenge the destroyed cities and the dead people.

Witzliwitle said,

'Prove your bravery! Go to the mountain where the leader of all tigers lives! Each of these leaders is named after Shere Khin. Fight him. Defeat him. Bring me his skin. Prove your courage! When you do, your names shall remain in history forever.'"

The Quartermaster left you a brief translation of the June tablet.
"The man and the girl were walking through deserted lands and barrens for a long time. They were headed to the June cities far away from their village. The road was hard. They had to survive on cactus fruit. They came across a cunning jackal, a poisonous snake, and a vampire bat. But they defeated all of them with their skills.

They arrived at the city and started looking for help to get revenge. However, no one was willing to fight gigantic fire dragons. People only cared about their own lives. Finally, they arrived at the remote city on the edge of the great forest.

'Our building will never turn to dust,' the ruler of the city said. 'We have a lot of shelters and places to hide. The rocks will help see the hidden ways.'"

Marianna Lopatina's Log.

June 16, 1018

Arrived at Eljune today. Going to look for June artifacts. Rumor has it, goblins have recently found a stash full of journals. However, all these coon care about is gold. They'd take the coins and throw away the clay tablets. There's a fat chance I can find something really interesting! If all goes well, everyone will soon forget the prankster.

P.S. I hear there's a place famous for its drinks. I'd better check it out first, see if anyone tries to pay with June coins.

Marianna Lopatina's Log.

June 27, 1018

Ha, I knew the June city ruins are a real treasure with all their secrets! Apparently, over the years, the Historians would have taken everything. But wait, after spending several minutes among the columns I found several stashes!

Here's a brief translation of the June's journal.

"I'm so happy! I'm thanking gods! I've found my family that I thought I'd lost forever!

I thought they were dead, my dear wife and children. But I found them among the smoldering ruins of June Itsmal! We all gathered here under the leadership of the brave Tka-a-Lithan Ric-ti-a-Nic to decide what to do next.

We have a near-even split. Some say we should run, others insist we should stay and talk to the Dark. We have several days before the curse comes back. For now, it's aiming at the other cities. Smoke is rising above our cities along the coast...

We must hurry and make up our minds. The skies, waters, and woods will witness our decision. Oh gods help us select the right path."

Curious... This looks like the last tablet from the ruins. Goblins must have taken the rest. I wonder where the next part of the story is. How can I know what the Junes decided it their only witnesses were "the skies, waters, and woods"?

Any other witnesses would have fled somewhere southeast, away from the darkness.

If only the trees could talk...

Marianna Lopatina's Log.

June 29, 1018

This is getting dangerous. Someone's been hunting for my journal. It's the goblins I escaped from. Now they're after me.
Fortunately, I found a network of demonic portals while trying to learn about the June history. It gives me some time to think where to go next.

We're aware that the Curse was, apparently, one of the first demons. Who could tell me about them? I need a pro.

Marianna Lopatina's Log.

July 1, 1018

I found a pilgrim, who is also a Demon Hunter among other things!

And I say, he's got a keen eye! He knows his way around demons, like he has a nose for them.

The Hunter told me that he found ruins with traces of a demon so powerful that even Octulhu would be like a kitten to a tiger. He said that the battle of this demon and a mage had bent the earth. Over time, water accumulated there.

I wonder if I can find this place. My search might be coming to an end!

Marianna Lopatina's Log.

July 2, 1018

The water was freezing! It was a miracle that I didn't turn to ice in this cold water.

It's a good thing I bought the magimeter in the port. Without it, I couldn't find out anything.

It's true. There was a battle where the lake is. The curse has landed on the June survivors again. And the June mage had to fight him. His most powerful spells could only delay the enemy for a while.

The curse was trapped in ice. Junes had only a few minutes. They ran... higher and higher.

The mage stayed to make another curse.

Marianna Lopatina's Log.

June 17, 1018

Lucky me! Found a couple of tablets. On to translating them now. It's curious. These records belong to the Junes that lived here when their civilization fell. I don't quite understand the text, but I know the words about the darkness and death. It looks like a battle... and a giant golem seems to be involved. Then it mentions the Curse. Has the author lost their family and run? The note stops abruptly.

I asked around about the other tablets. Apparently, some pilgrim was collecting them. Ugh, another saint! He went on and on about how he wanted to visit the place where the greatest miracle had happened, the first resurrection!

I've got to visit this place.

My beloved Nancy!

I'm leaving you this note in case you'll be looking for me. Our holy father Ivan, the Devotee, gave me advice to visit the place known for its holiness. The first Chapel of Tensess! A great miracle happened here. Suddenly, an evil astral demon appeared and smashed the ship! But those who died in astral were brought back to life by the grace of Tensess. They appeared right here!

The chapel is locked and abandoned. It upsets me greatly. I know that Goblins are to blame! They're wicked creatures, thieves and hustlers! I heard an interesting story about them, though. They say that the ship that got wrecked in astral was carrying two goblins. They went into the Purgatory. One of them saw a Servant of Tensess and got scared! He started confessing his sins, promising to sacrifice mirra. The other goblin heard that and offered to sell mirra! And it's been like this ever since: one goblin received Tensess's forgiveness and became a gift collector; the other goblin was cursed and banished from the Purgatory forever.

Well, one way or the other, my beloved Nancy, I should visit the smugglers. Have a row with them. Why have they neglected the Chapel? The mongers have the guts to collect money from pilgrims! Their leader lives somewhere around here. He takes ughing sessions on a meadow, whatever that means. I'll give them an ughing session!

I will see you soon, my darling. I miss you. I'll return to you as soon as I sort this thing out.

Marianna Lopatina's Log.

June 18, 1018

I'm so angry! It took me a while to catch this idiot! Thank Tensess, I've got the tablets now. And this is the missing part!

I restored the missing fragment. It's a story of the great fall of the city June Itsmal.

"For the city was great and the citizens were proud. Gifts were brought to June Itsmal from all over the world.   Beautiful ships arrived at Takalik harbor. June Itsmal ruler, the great Xolocipilli, was brave and wise. He used to kill the fire dragons.

Everything changed in one day. The Curse came to the city. The walls were tall, the gates were strong, but all defenses fell. The Curse took lives with just one stare. Mighty golems taller than the tallest trees have come to battle. But even they couldn't stop the Curse. The towers fell. Xolocipilli's palace fell and buried the city ruler underneath. Only a few survivors escaped the ruins of June Itsmal in the dead of night.

What happened next? Whoever wrote this, they clearly survived! I need to find the next piece...

I asked around if anything interesting was found lately. People tell me that they saw one girl of easy virtue bragging about a pretty stone with strange inscriptions.  Not much of a trace, but that's all I have.

Boy, it never gets old.

Marianna Lopatina's Log.

June 19, 1018

I think I'm onto something. An elf told me about a battle between goblins and the Free Traders' Mercenaries that took place recently. That was rough.

Louis also shared a couple of useful contacts. Someone's been hunting June artifacts. And that someone was spotted asking the mercenaries about any interesting recent findings. Perhaps, he was the one to hire goblins.

Well, anyway, those bastards wanted to break into Asee-Teph. The fight was furious! Rocks falling everywhere, arrows flying around, swords clinking. I wish I could see it!

Unfortunately, this means that those tablet will be very hard to find.

Among the notes about different things, from the shape of Eljune stones to Ammer centaurs, you find a note addressed to someone. It says, "Dear friend! I know making a decision is hard. I'm setting camp not far away from here, near the sand anomaly. You can find me there if you change your mind."

A series of blurry images brings you a gibberling's cunning face. You immediately realize that this is the one you've been looking for! You can't see his partners in the fog, but there's one phrase you can make out, "Termites? That's nothing! Anyone could beat them! They're just tiny insects." You're keeping this memory for a long time.

The letter says,

"Why, of course! A brilliant thief ends up like a rat in a trap. Because you need to think twice before obeying someone!

"I'll tip you off a place, and you bring me the merch."

I found nothing wrong with the things that were going too smoothly! A Historian with the necessary artifact, the information about a secret anomaly at the right moment. Listen, whoever you are. I have no idea what this creature is, but he isn't what he seems. He isn't just a huge guy.

If he offers you a deal, and by chance you've been following my footsteps, you better run. Run, because at some point he won't need you anymore, and you'll end up... ...well, like me. It's not that I regret this, but I was planning to live a little longer. So, he miniaturized me, I got in the cave to fetch the "amazing artifact", and he just left me here... Alright, take care. And good luck. At least, someone should have good luck."

You open the letter and read, "It's time to say goodbye, my friend. Sometimes you were harsh, but we had great time together. I'm heading West through the lands of ogres. They could tell me a hundred times that I'm stupid, that nothing but death awaits me, but I'm sure there's something good inside every being. Good luck!"

The letter is written in dancing letters. "You must be good if you could survive the damned storm! Sorry, but I already emptied out this place. I don't know who you are, but I could make use of people like you. I'm going to the goblins' leader to sell the stuff. Check out his location. With a little luck, I will still be there. My messenger should be waiting for me in the hollow by the pier.
I was scared at first. Then I got drunk and dived head first into the arch between the stones. I'm not sure what went straight to my head, the booze or the...

This letter has been written just recently. Unfortunately, the ink has bled with humidity. The letter is barely readable.
"Hello, Ad***, m* l**e.

I th**k, I man***ed to find **** you **** looking ***. The anc**** J*** tabl*t s***ng some**ing ab*ut T**-R** you t**k int***st in l**ely. It c*st me * ni*ht of l**e with an arc*****gist.

I'm k*ep**g it for a wh***. Vis*t me ** ** swa*p ** you w**t to *ee it.

***** yours, Nad* ** *****."

Who is this mysterious Nad? Nada? Nadashti? Nadir?

name.en: List of goods on the ship

description.en: There's a detailed drawing of different types of termites, including plagued and modified, along with a brief note, "Akto Nuntley could control Tlacattls, but not Tlatoanim."
There's a detailed drawing of termites' victims, wrapped up for storage, along with a brief note, "Tlatoanim exercised absolute power over Maitls."
There's a detailed drawing of an intermediate species between a human and a termite, along with a brief note, "Any Tlacattl would obey Yk Ome Nuntley and Yk Hey Nuntley."

I didn't expect Polis to be such an amazing place. Aoidos managed to build so many things here. What a gifted nation! Just like us.

I came across a weird vagabond who was looking for something, mumbling nonsense. I tried to run away, but he just wouldn't leave me alone! One thing led to another, and here we are, relaxing after exploring this city's every nook and cranny. To understand how much fun we had, just imagine how hard it is for a CENTAUR to climb onto a roof. I'm not sure I can repeat that!

My friend loves secrecy and conspiracies! Poor fellow, he just can't see past these mysteries. I should remember to leave him a note about my future plans. It should make him happy.

I'm sorry to leave you, my friend, but the road's a-callin'.

Besides, even if I stay, can a centaur find a job in Polis? This is how it is...

You've helped me realize something. If you keep searching, you'll eventually find something. I didn't know that at first, but then I understood. You just have a goal and strive to reach it. It doesn't matter what other people think. It requires strong will. Above all, don't lose yourself while to solve another mystery!

Perhaps our paths will cross later. If you're interested, I'm heading to the South of Dion Mountain Range, beyond the Pearl Slopes, to see those demons people keep talking about.

Demons are amazing. I didn't expect them to be this beautiful. They use images to communicate. Images appear directly in your head. Isn't it wonderful? It's weird how many people might consider them evil or dark creatures. Of course, they can scare you, and they can't take a joke, but they are so, so beautiful!

People despise rats as well, but have rats ever hurt anyone? They're living beings who want their share of food and water! Hardly any rat ever crawled inside a house with malicious intent!

Some demons never heard of centaurs, so I left a note to the most curious of them. He gave me something in exchange...

This is a lovely place. I'll sleep it off here, and then I'll head to Triquetrum. Aoidos mentioned "energies" there. I need to see them.

I think I know what Aoidos meant by "energies". We'd say this place was "blessed by the spirits". They might have over-blessed it a bit. Everything here seems ordinary and miraculous at the same time.

The most interesting places are never talked about. You only get to know them by chance: overhear a conversation or spot a turn in the road... I'm getting more and more confident that I made the right decision. You can't just sit around peacefully when there's a big world outside with so much to see!

I hope some other strange adventurer who finds my notes and follows my tracks will never regret their decision!

I discovered that I left my favorite toy behind. It's not that important, but it holds so many good memories. I'll drop by our camp tonight. Just need to make sure not to run into my sister or friends.

Just think about it. No two-legged creature can imagine how hard it is to sneak quietly on four muscular legs.

I got carried away and walked through the whole the camp! I can't brag about it to anyone, but it's something I can write down in my notes!

Familiar places look different at night. You get to notice things you never noticed before. It makes you understand things you couldn't until now. But enough of "philosophizing", as Aoidos used to say.

My sister was asleep as I grabbed the toy. I think she sensed my presence but never woke up. I don't know how. She might have sighed in a special way. I grew up with her, so I can feel her with my heart.

I know she will forgive me. She won't think I escaped.

There's only one place left to visit. It's the Site of Power. They say that the swords are always clashing there. I'll go to the champions' camp and get myself drunk to leave these lands without a second thought.

All right, the swords here aren't always clashing. I didn't see a single battle while I was here. I guess I was incredibly lucky.

Boy, did we get drunk! I couldn't imagine so many people can ride my back all at once! An idea of giving people rides never occurred to me in the first place.

I received a mug with my name on it - somebody carved it with a knife. I was called "a great man and an average horse". They also invited me to stop by whenever I'm around. I will stop by on my way back, perhaps.

They say alcohol won't solve your problems. It sure won't, but a good party can chase away the gloom. It's important to maintain the balance... It's very important.

I'm going to the Dionic Archipelago. I've heard a lot of wonderful things about it. I'll see you on the docks, my imaginable follower.

It turns out, I'm fond of villages, no matter who lives there (unless it's someone who wants to rip out your guts). They all look alike in a way. Whatever happens in the world, they live their own lives, look after their households, be it centaurs or humans...

I'm getting more and more romantic. I wonder if the travels induced this in me, or if it's an adventurer's disease, common for all wanderers. I neither can nor want to figure it out! I think I'll just go with the flow.

I've been dreaming about lying alone on a pasture, far away from home, without knowing what lies ahead, simply admiring the stars. It's time to make the dream come true. Let me find the nearest pasture and head right there.

So, I've been watching the sunset. I'm writing this note while the sun is still up, so I wouldn't ruin a starry night by scribbling things down.

Whenever the stars are seen, I don't feel like writing. They make you feel so small and unimportant... You start thinking about what's happening up there, the amazing and significant events.

I'm feeling nostalgic. I suddenly remembered my sis and my dear village. How are they doing back home? I'm not homesick, but it'd be nice to know that they are doing fine.

Back to real life tomorrow. I'm taking part in all kinds of local entertainment - as a spectator at first. I'm going to Coliseum in the morning. In the meantime...

My request to participate made the jaws drop. They tried to talk me out of it, but their leader decided that a Centaur riding a Pegasus was a great publicity. He gave me the most powerful stallion!

Now picture their faces when I took out a piece of parchment and started scribbling, right up in the air, on the Pegasus's back! As if I were an incredible poet of ancient times! That's what I'm doing right now. The parchment crackles and leaps out of my hands. There's too much magic here! I don't know if I can hold it. Got to find something calmer after the flight. Like a local maze, where you can easily get lost...

I can't quite understand where I am. All turns look the same. Here's a gazebo, and there's another one. I sat down to collect my thoughts while I'm writing another note.

After my spectacular ride, they allowed me to take part in other activities. I'm a local star - or, maybe, a local crazy. Go figure!

This place is... creepy. Not only paths, but thoughts get twisted here. Someone evil created this place. Someone, who enjoys watching helpless wavering. Why on earth did I come here? And these Minotaurs... are staring. Some would say, we're alike, but it's hard to imagine two more different species if you ask me.

I must choose something simpler next time. An obstacle course, for example. The whole trick is to run to the final line and finish first. Unsophisticated, but fun!

Now I should find the way out. In the end, they might remember to find me and get me out of here... I hope.

Yay, I was the best! ...in kicking down the obstacles. No surprise. It's made for the two-legged.

I rushed towards the end, kicking down every obstacle in my way. I was so angry! Tried to be careful, of course, not to hurt anyone. It's a good thing I was running behind everyone else.

They were waiting for me at the finish line to let me cross it first as a sign of respect. No way, I thought. So I pushed the well-mannered Aoidoi beyond the finish line by force! They deserved this victory, so let them take it!

I'll balance the loss at the race. That's where I'll finish first!

Oh spirits, I don't know what to say! Some places and events just change your very essence over an instant! The Observatory took my breath away.

I learned a lot. They told me about other worlds, about Architects and time travel, about the endless astral. News like this take time to digest.

It will take even longer to see it all!

Whoever is reading this note, I'll say goodbye. I don't know where I'm going, but it's somewhere far away. I'm looking for... I don't know what, but I must find it.

Go your own way. I'm sure it will be legendary. If you want it, of course.

I left a gift for my reader. Find the small crate. It contains the most needful thing.

Take it with you. In a way, I'm grateful. It was a journey that we took together.

Good luck, whoever you are.

It is an old letter, scribbled on a piece of parchment, or rather, on a piece of rough leather.

Nevertheless, you can recognize the Aoidos language, written by a strong hand, not used to writing.

I was too arrogant to ignore my aches... I hit my head on a branch and twisted two ankles! Thank the spirits it happened near the camp. The locals helped me and gave me food and water. They also told me a lot of stories. It almost feels like home.

I didn't leave home just to settle down somewhere else, even in a nice place like this. I looked at the sky and felt that my heart was full. The open road is calling my name again. Where should I head? I remembered the story of Kyros and Aellona. Kyros, the poor fellow, defeated our chief and earned the tribe's respect... After Aellona died, he went mad and messed up everything. Such a sad story, but also beautiful. I could write a song about it.

I decided to visit Aellona's grave. I'll leave in the morning.

Oh spirits, I have the strangest feeling. It's like guilt for being alive when Aellona is dead. Enough of being sad, though. I should leave a note in a safe place, away from prying eyes...

I'm asking myself why I'm doing this. Do I want to leave a trail? Do I secretly hope that someone might follow my tracks? Do I expect someone to find me? My sister, a secret admirer, or just someone simply wandering around the world?

Since I started making notes, I should continue. Now I'm wondering where it will take me!

It cheered me up. Where will I go next? I think I'll visit Polis. It isn't far from here. I heard it was a lovely place full of people. Maybe I can find a friend there.

This Magic Tablecloth can produce dainty dishes as well as magic potions that increase Proficiency and Vitality.

Can be used 4 times a day and once in 15 minutes at most.

Disappears after 30 days.
A large number of small birds are roughly drawn on paper, and below them - a surprised fish. The fish looks familiar. Something unusual must have happened on the Tropical Atoll.

In earlier days, one had to carry one's own magic astrolabe. With the development of astralnautics, astrolabes were integrated into the ship's systems, and now jumps can be made while using the astral charts onboard the ship.

The writing is barely readable, but the one thing is clear: somebody named Rajah suggests that Vizir should order a fruit basket for Guzel's eighteenth anniversary. It'd be a good idea to have a word with this Rajah...

The letter was written in a neat handwriting. The author was probably a woman. First, she blamed Alister for evasiveness, then threatened him, and then pleaded him to change his mind and fulfill some promise.

Passionate and optimistic call for assistance with preparations of the Anniversary event. Contains accurate praise of your own guild.

Upon reading, grants you 10 Loyalty and 50.000 Prestige. To read it, you need to be in a guild. Can be read only in capital city of your faction.

Shorter passionate and optimistic call for assistance with preparations of the Anniversary event. Contains accurate praise of your own guild.

Upon reading, grants you 1 Loyalty and 10.000 Prestige. To read it, you need to be in a guild. Can be read only in capital city of your faction.

Provides access to mailbox, bank, auction and Currency Exchange; teleports to any location, buys items and sells Mirra.

When used, summons a Master Goblin who offers these services. Only the character that summons the Goblin can interact with him!

The goblin will remain for 10 minutes after being summoned.

Can't be summoned on Evermeet Isle by League characters, in the Cloud Nine Health Resort by Imperial characters, and on Howlem.

Goods from the Boutique.

According to Panto de Ardeur, the palace gondolier, there were no strange flights from the palace and the House de Vevre’s residence.

According to Tilbert de Ardeur, the gondolier of the northern districts, there were no strange flights from the districts and the House de Delice’s residence.

According to Tassilon de Ardeur, the port gondolier, there were no strange flights from the port, but there were some from the House de Delice’s residence.

According to Alice de Ardeur, the gondolier of the House de Vevre's residence, there were no strange flights from the residence, but there were some from the northern districts.

According to Josephine de Ardeur, the gondolier of the House de Delice's residence, there were no strange flights from them and the House de Blizare’s residence.

According to Sherman de Ardeur, the gondolier of the House de Blizare's residence, there were no strange flights from them, but there were some from the House de Delice’s residence.

We know for certain that only Panto de Ardeur and Tilbert de Ardeur can be trusted.

Someone must have dropped it because they were in a hurry. On the last pages, you read: "...Day 13. I noticed that the general had been waiting for someone since the beginning of the expedition, but I didn't dare ask. Today a sentry returned from patrol, looking alarmed. I eavesdropped on their conversation. We'll break camp today and move deeper into the snow, somewhere towards the mountains in Silent Toroses. A Lamia squad is tracking us... Why are they here? What do they want with us? So many questions..."

The note in neat handwriting reads:

The Great Ball is a demonstration of the accomplishments of all the Great Houses of elves. At each of the Great Balls, one of the Houses showed something grandiose. It all began when the elves recovered from the past Cataclysm, created portals on their allods, and started visiting each other.

Year 265, House de Doucer wins. Great Mage Gramont di Douceur, with the consent of the other Heads of the Houses, creates new rules for the Great Balls. The first Great Ball takes place on the Yoggor allod.

Year 275, House de Vevre wins, Orelina de Vevre writes the poem "The World's End" that describes the history of the Cataclysm and the subsequent events. The second Great Ball was also held on the Yoggor allod, but later it was decided to hold the Ball on the allod of the winner of the last Ball.

The note in neat handwriting reads:

Year 305, House de Desirae wins, Great Mage Margot de Desirae writes "Dialogues on Service", substantiating a point of view that explains why elves should educate lower races and have them serve elves. Those who are resistant to training (humans in particular) should be avoided.

Year 319, House de Blizare wins. Great Mage Bernard de Blizare creates "The Treatise on the Essence of the Astral", with a theoretical substantiation of the existence of the Astral.

Year 335, House de Grandeur wins, Vincent de Grandeur creates "The Book of Astral Curses" which summarizes all known spells associated with the astral.

Year 364, House de Delice wins. Ervier de Delice invents a stable stationary portal between the allods that allows you to travel in a relatively simple way, albeit with a colossal expenditure of magical energy.

Year 384, House de Desirae wins. Viola di Desirae writes "Odes of Love", a collection of the greatest elven love lyrics.

The note in neat handwriting reads:

Year 404, House de Delice wins. Florian de Delice finds a solution to the dispute between the elven Houses and settles the conflict over territory.

Year 419, House de Doucer wins, Renalda de Doucer restores the list of ancient elven spells found on Yoggor.

Year 443, House de Delice wins/ Florian de Delice solves the problem of settling the status of the Small elven Houses.

Year 464, House de Pluie wins. Thibault de Pluie creates an economic treatise on trade, banks and auctions.

Year 479, House de Ardeur wins, Gaben de Ardeur makes a breakthrough in the study of the properties of June crystals.

Year 499, House de Pluie wins, Gracienna de Pluie creates a unique piece of jewelry - the Diadem of Drops.

The note in neat handwriting reads:

Year 515, House de Blizare wins, Justine de Blizare completes a study on the influence of the astral on the flora and fauna of allods.

Year 538, House de Vevre wins. Majel de Vevre writes an opera about Irene, one of the greatest works in the genre.

Year 556, House de Grandeur wins, Neven de Grandeur writes a work on the history of magic from the founding of the elven kingdom to the present day.

Year 583, House de Desirae wins, Rival de Desirae creates a ten-ingredient salad recipe.

Year 596, House de Delice wins. Denise de Delice paints one of the most beautiful paintings in history - The Birth of Beauty, depicting the awakening of the first elves.

The note in neat handwriting reads:

Year 800, House de Grandeur win. Albert de Grandeur will settle the conflict between the Kanians and Gibberlings, then enter into an alliance with them. The Gibberlings receive the Lightwood allod in exchange for the secret of astral flights.

Year 823, House de Ardeur wins, Raymond de Ardeur creates the prototype of the first astral ship.

Year 845, House de Blizare wins, Maximilien de Blizare invents a new potion that greatly speeds up reactions.

Year 864, House de Pluie wins. Guillaume de Pluie formulates the principles of cultural expansion, which should transform other civilizations, passing to them the ideals of the elves. Elves finally step out of isolation.

Year 884, House de Vevre wins. Caspar de Vevre writes the Triumph of Beauty symphony, one of the greatest works of the elves.

The note in neat handwriting reads:

Year 901, House de Doucer wins. Umbert de Doucer comes up with a plan of attack on the Kirah allod and starts a new war with the Empire. Astral ships will be used in this war.

Year 924, House de Blizare wins. After repelling an attack of astral demons, Great Mage Maximilien de Blizare writes a military work about their vulnerabilities and the ways of dealing with them. In the future, this information becomes the basis for the creation of the Order of Demon Hunters.

Year 937, House de Grandeur wins, Estelle di Grander predicts the future. Recorded, her predictions become known as Estelle's Quatrains. The Conclave decides to classify some of the information they contain. Estelle's prophecies rehabilitate the elven Oracles who are now free to practice.

Year 958, House de Ardeur wins. Raymond de Ardeur and his student Celestina de Ardeur solve the mystery of the Imperial astral energy and improve its principles.

Year 990, House de Desirae wins, Dakkar de Desirae demonstrates extraordinary skills in the field of necromancy. From that moment on, the Conclave finally lifts the prohibitions on necromancy.
A letter written by Gerda invites you to return to Isa and visit her, her brothers, and other Gibberlings who have new tasks and rewards for you.

Fragment of the Carpet of Fate from Skalgard. The pattern woven on it depicts an astral ship flying in the sky above Isa. The edges cut with sharp scissors are not frayed at all - Koll took good care of his treasure.

Required for the quest: Full Picture.

name.en: Sixth Fragment of the Carpet of Fate

description.en:
I believe you've been waiting for word from me for some time, ...

The time has come. The barricades at the exits from the city have been removed - Hirkalla's guards have driven off most of the distorted creatures.

It means we can move on - if you remember, we still need to find five more "odd people out" whose fates have been stolen.

Please, hurry – the sooner we continue our search, the greater our chances of success.
The long and rather tedious letter contains a list of changes that Ilya Oblomov is thinking of introducing on his estate, as well as a number of issues related to farming in the village of Oblomovka.
This diary contains the record of the greatest experiment in Sarnaut's history. An experiment that ended in the Cataclysm and brought the whole word to the edge of destruction!

Overlord Nezeb has been preparing to return to his former homeland for a long time. He subjugated all tribes of the desert and the entire south! Numerous forges were forging weapons from raw materials that came from quarries and ore mines scattered here and there in the desert.

name.en: The Chronicles of the Great Nezeb's Reign: "On the Founding of Xadagan", Part 1

description.en: Numerous mages worked to enchant this weapon, for the Xadaganians had to battle the Kanians who had their own mages. The strongest of them formed the Conclave, and now the Great Nezeb had to use all his power to challenge the Kanian dogs and win!

name.en: The Chronicles of the Great Nezeb's Reign: "On the Founding of Xadagan", Part 2

description.en: The Great Nezeb had a special weapon - a secret guarded so carefully that I do not dare speak of it. Its power terrified his allies as it was not created by a human hand but through ancient mysterious sorcery alien to humans. But the Great Nezeb, the most cunning and powerful of us, was able to wield this power, and it greatly aided the preparations for the war...

name.en: The Chronicles of the Great Nezeb's Reign: "On the Founding of Xadagan", Part 3

description.en: So numerous were the weapons collected, so heavy the chests of gold and jewelry, that no caravan was able to carry this cargo out of the desert within a reasonable time. Fate dictated that the Great Nezeb should leave part of his treasures here, in the desert. Thankfully one of his allies was willing to guard these treasures... His name was the Gray Prince...

name.en: The Chronicles of the Great Nezeb's Reign: "On the Founding of Xadagan", Part 4
